regs.name: SoC Control Register
regs.desc: Board-level control (mbv_soc_top). Core is held in reset while core_run=0; load RAM and configure the encoder first, then set core_run=1.

fields.name: core_run
fields.desc: 1: release the MicroBlaze V core from reset (run). 0: hold core in reset.
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: trace_clear
fields.desc: 1: clear the trace capture buffer and byte/beat counters.
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: trace_flush
fields.desc: 1: assert ATB flush (afvalid) so the encoder drains buffered trace.
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: irq_gen_en
fields.desc: 1: enable HW IRQ pulse generator (1-cycle pulse every 4096 clks ~ 55 us @75 MHz) into the core's external interrupt (G6 hardening).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: cva6_run
fields.desc: 1: release the CVA6 core (soc2) from reset. Independent of core_run: set only AFTER the program was loaded into the reserved PS-DDR window at 0x6400_0000 (devmem; docs/SPEC_board_memory_map.md).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: core0_run
fields.desc: 1: release core 0 alone (tgc5b2: TGC5B-0, duo/trio: MicroBlaze V). Effective run state is core_run | core0_run, so b0 still starts everything. Reads 0 on single-core designs and on pre-U1 bitstreams.
fields.access_rule: freely writable; the RAM window of THIS core is only accessible while its effective run bit is 0 -- an access to the RAM of a running core never gets ready and HANGS the AXI transaction (SPEC §10 point 2)

fields.name: core1_run
fields.desc: 1: release core 1 alone (tgc5b2: TGC5B-1, duo/trio: TGC5B). Effective run state is core_run | core1_run. Reads 0 on single-core designs and on pre-U1 bitstreams.
fields.access_rule: freely writable; the RAM window of THIS core is only accessible while its effective run bit is 0 (SPEC §10 point 2)

fields.name: cva6_run2
fields.desc: trio only: second release bit of the CVA6, OR-ed with the historic b5 cva6_run (trio_soc_top.sv:234). Exists so all three cores have a bit in the same b8..b10 field; b5 keeps working unchanged.
fields.access_rule: freely writable; alias of b5 (effective cva6_run = b5 | b10)

regs.name: SoC Status Register
regs.desc: Board-level status (read-only).

fields.name: trace_wrapped
fields.desc: 1: the trace capture RING buffer has wrapped at least once -- the oldest beats were overwritten (capture continues; nothing stalls). Clear via CONTROL.trace_clear.
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: axis_overflow
fields.desc: 1: AXIS capture BRAM overflowed.
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: core0_running
fields.desc: 1: core 0 is effectively released (CONTROL.core_run | CONTROL.core0_run). Reads 0 on pre-U1 bitstreams.
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: core1_running
fields.desc: 1: core 1 is effectively released (CONTROL.core_run | CONTROL.core1_run). Reads 0 on pre-U1 bitstreams.
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: cva6_running
fields.desc: trio only: 1 = the CVA6 is effectively released (CONTROL.cva6_run | CONTROL.cva6_run2).
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: Trace Beats Counter
regs.desc: Total captured ATB beats since last trace_clear (monotonic, does NOT stop at the ring capacity). Ring write position = TRACE_BEATS % (TRACE_BUFSZ/4).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: ATB beats captured since last trace_clear (monotonic).
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: Trace Bytes Counter
regs.desc: Total captured ATB bytes since last trace_clear (monotonic). Poll delta = live trace bandwidth.

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: ATB bytes captured since last trace_clear (monotonic).
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: AXIS Beats Counter
regs.desc: Number of captured AXIS beats (read-only).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: AXIS beats captured since last trace_clear.
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: Trace Ring Capacity
regs.desc: Capacity of the ATB trace capture ring buffer in bytes (read-only; 1 MiB URAM in the G7 build). Reads 0 on pre-ring bitstreams.

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Ring capacity in bytes (TRACE_DEPTH * 4).
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: Trace Sink Control
regs.desc: Enables/config of the additional trace sinks (DDR4 + PIB). Both sinks observe the funnel-merged ATB stream in parallel to the URAM ring and never back-pressure the trace path (own FIFO + drop counters).

fields.name: ddr_en
fields.desc: 1: DDR4 sink enabled (writes beats to PS DDR at DDR_BASE).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: ddr_clear
fields.desc: W1 pulse (only while ddr_en=0): reset DDR_WPTR/full/wrapped/err/drops -- and SINK_STAT.ddr_cfg_rej, the refusal marker of the U6 window interlock.
fields.access_rule: write-1 pulse: self-clearing, always reads back 0; clear only while ddr_en=0 -- the hardware does NOT enforce that, a pulse during an active capture resets its counters

fields.name: ddr_circ
fields.desc: DDR capture mode: 0 = one shot (stop when full), 1 = circular (wrap modulo DDR_SIZE, keeps the most recent bytes; write offset = DDR_WPTR % DDR_SIZE). Switch only while cleared.
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: uram_oneshot
fields.desc: URAM trace buffer mode: 0 = circular ring (default, keeps the most recent 1 MiB), 1 = one shot (capture stops when full, keeps the FIRST 1 MiB; SINK_STAT.uram_stopped sets).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: pib_en
fields.desc: 1: PIB parallel trace port enabled (pib_clk runs, beats serialized).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: pib_clear
fields.desc: W1 pulse (only while pib_en=0): reset PIB drop counter.
fields.access_rule: write-1 pulse: self-clearing, always reads back 0; the hardware does NOT enforce the pib_en=0 rule (ct_trace_sinks.sv:125,142-146)

fields.name: pib_calib
fields.desc: 1: PIB emits the calibration pattern instead of trace (reference trPibCalibrate); the trace input is not consumed.
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: pib_div
fields.desc: PIB port clock divider: pib_clk = clk / 2^(div+1); 0 is clamped to 1 (max 18.75 MHz @75 MHz core -> 18.75 MB/s byte rate).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: pib_pattern
fields.desc: Calibration pattern (reference trPibCalibPattern): 0 = STANDARD (AA 55 00 FF), 1 = MOVING_ONE (walking 1), 2 = MOVING_ZERO (walking 0).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

regs.name: Trace Funnel Control
regs.desc: Per-channel arbitration priority of the message-atomic trace funnel (ct_L1_funnel, MAX_PRIO=3). Higher value wins on message boundaries; equal values arbitrate round-robin. Live-writable (takes effect at the next message boundary). The reference-PIB funnel CSRs (trFunnelArbMode/Shed*) are not part of this build.

fields.name: prio_ch0
fields.desc: Priority of channel 0 (Encoder 0, MBV).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: prio_ch1
fields.desc: Priority of channel 1 (Encoder 1, TGC5B).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: prio_ch2
fields.desc: Priority of channel 2 (Encoder 2, CVA6).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: te_tag_always
fields.desc: E-Trace mode: emit a source tag in front of EVERY packet instead of only after a channel switch (funnel te_tag_always). No effect in N-Trace mode.
fields.access_rule: freely writable; the register write mask is 0x0001_0333 -- bits outside it are dropped silently

regs.name: DDR Sink Base Address
regs.desc: Byte address of the linear DDR capture buffer in PS DDR (32-byte aligned; low bits are masked). Reset 0x5000_0000 = start of the reserved PL window 0x5000_0000..0x6FFF_FFFF (512 MiB, no-map via ctrace_resmem.dtso; docs/SPEC_board_memory_map.md address plan v4) for every ct_trace_sinks design (tgc5b2/duo/trio, package U6) and for rocket2. The tops that still wire their own sink (rocket, cva6_2, cva6_linux, cva6_linux64) reset to 0x6000_0000 -- read the register, do not assume it. Keep inside the reserved window when reconfiguring.

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: PS DDR byte address (32-byte aligned).
fields.access_rule: READ-ONLY BY POLICY in the dashboard (U9): the window is fixed by the bitstream reset and by the boot reserved-memory region -- /api/write answers 403 for this register, and the panel shows it without an input field. The HARDWARE is weaker: a write while the sink is armed is REFUSED (U6 interlock, SINK_STAT b4 ddr_cfg_rej), but at ddr_en=0 it is taken, and on the older tops with their own sink wiring it is taken even while the AXI write master is RUNNING

regs.name: DDR Sink Buffer Size
regs.desc: Capture buffer size in bytes (multiple of 4; configurable from the DDR panel). Reset 0x1000_0000 (256 MiB, address plan v4: the trace window 0x5000_0000..0x5FFF_FFFF, 64 MiB clear of the guest code window at 0x6400_0000). The tops with their own sink wiring still reset to 0x0400_0000 (64 MiB). One shot: when full, SINK_STAT.ddr_full sets and further beats are dropped (counted). Circular: write offset wraps modulo this size.

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Buffer size in bytes; 0 disables writes.
fields.access_rule: READ-ONLY BY POLICY in the dashboard (U9): a size that reaches past the reserved region is as dangerous as a wrong base -- /api/write answers 403 for this register and the panel shows it without an input field. The HARDWARE is weaker: a write while the sink is armed is REFUSED (U6 interlock, SINK_STAT b4 ddr_cfg_rej, it would let one burst escape the buffer), but at ddr_en=0 it is taken, and on the older tops with their own sink wiring it changes the wrap point of a RUNNING capture

regs.name: DDR Sink Write Pointer
regs.desc: TOTAL bytes written since last ddr_clear (monotonic, read-only). One shot: host reads [DDR_BASE, DDR_BASE+min(WPTR,SIZE)). Circular: write offset = WPTR % SIZE; chronological order = [off..SIZE) ++ [0..off) once wrapped (same contract as the URAM ring).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Bytes written (completed AXI bursts only).
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: Trace Sink Status
regs.desc: Sink status flags (read-only; DDR bits cleared by ddr_clear).

fields.name: ddr_full
fields.desc: 1: DDR buffer full in one-shot mode; further beats drop.
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: ddr_axi_err
fields.desc: 1: an AXI write returned BRESP != OKAY (sticky).
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: ddr_wrapped
fields.desc: 1: circular DDR buffer wrapped at least once (oldest bytes overwritten).
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: uram_stopped
fields.desc: 1: URAM one-shot capture stopped (buffer full, first 1 MiB kept).
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: ddr_cfg_rej
fields.desc: 1: a DDR_BASE/DDR_SIZE write was REFUSED because the sink was armed (ddr_en=1) -- sticky until ddr_clear (U6 window interlock, ct_trace_sinks.sv). Reads 0 on the pre-U6 bitstreams and on the tops that wire their own sink; there the write is taken over while the master runs.
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: DDR Sink Dropped Beats
regs.desc: Beats dropped by the DDR sink (FIFO overflow or buffer full; saturating; read-only).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Dropped beats since ddr_clear.
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: PIB Dropped Beats
regs.desc: Beats dropped by the PIB sink (FIFO overflow when the port rate is below the trace rate; saturating; read-only).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Dropped beats since pib_clear.
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: DDR Sink Beat Counter
regs.desc: Beats offered to the DDR sink while ddr_en (accepted = BEATS - DDR_DROPS; cleared by ddr_clear; read-only) -- the cheap proof that beats reach the sink at all. NOTE: this counter sat at 0x30 in the tgc5b2 C0B_DDR build; since the shared three-sink subsystem (T2, ct_trace_sinks) it lives at 0x38 for ALL designs and 0x30 is PIB_DROPS (docs/SPEC_axis_wp_memory_map.md §9).

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Beats offered to the DDR sink since ddr_clear.
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: CTTE Encoder Control Register
regs.desc: Primary control register for the CTTE Encoder

fields.name: Active
fields.desc: Primary enable/reset for the Trace Encoder
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: Enable
fields.desc:
1: Trace Encoder is enabled. Allows trTeInstTracing and
trTeDataTracing to turn tracing on and off. Setting trTeEnable to 0
flushes any queued trace data to the sink or funnel attached to this
encoder. This bit can be set to 1 only by direct writing to it. This write
of 1 should be done after all other settings are done.
Enable gates instruction and data tracing: effective instruction
tracing is (Enable AND trTeInstTracing). Clearing Enable therefore
implicitly disables instruction (and data) tracing without rewriting
those bits; the resulting instruction-tracing-disabled edge generates
the trace-off Program Trace Correlation Message (see trTeInstTracing).
[CTTE: the implicit-disable gating is RTL, not an RDL auto-clear.]
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: InstTracing
fields.desc:
Instruction trace generation. Effective instruction tracing is
(trTeControl.Enable AND this bit). The 1->0 edge of effective
instruction tracing (this bit cleared, or Enable cleared) makes the
encoder emit a Program Trace Correlation Message (TCODE 33,
EVCODE=Program Trace Disabled) carrying the residual instruction
count and branch history, so a decoder can resolve the final
instructions up to the trace-off point; the 0->1 edge emits a
TRACE_ENABLE synchronization message to re-anchor the decoder.
[CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: Empty
fields.desc: Reads as 1 when all generated trace has been emitted
fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: InstMode
fields.desc:
Instruction trace generation mode. Only accessible on trTeControl. Enable=0.
WARL: legal values are 6 (ITR_BRANCH_HIST, HTM) always, and 3
(ITR_BRANCH, BTM) iff the CT_EN_BTM build switch is set. With both
modes settable, N-Trace Table 8 ('3 OR 6 settable') is fully met.
A write of any illegal value is legalized to 6 before it reaches the
register; when CT_EN_BTM=0 a write of 3 is likewise legalized to 6
(honest 'BTM unsupported' read-back). Legalization lives in
ct_cs_cpuif_wb.sv (the Wishbone adapter), not in this generated
block. [CTTE specific]

3.name: ITR_BRANCH
3.desc: Generate instruction trace using Branch Trace Messaging (BTM: Nexus DirectBranch TCODE 3 / IndirectBranch TCODE 4 -- one message per taken/indirect branch). Legal iff the CT_EN_BTM build switch is set; otherwise WARL-legalized to 6.

6.name: ITR_BRANCH_HIST
6.desc: Generate instruction trace using Branch History Trace (HTM)

fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

fields.name: SendConfig
fields.desc:
Send NEXUS_MSG_VENDOR_CONFIG (TCODE 58) messages: the encoder
describes its compiled-in capabilities and runtime configuration
on-wire so a decoder can configure itself from the stream
(self-describing trace; payload layout in rtl/pkg/ct_pkg.sv).
Resets to CFG_ONCE in the full profile (AW E6, seq 24);
profiles without the feature read CFG_NONE. [CTTE specific]

1.name: CFG_ONCE
1.desc: Do send config message at trace start (rising edge of effective instruction tracing). Config changes require Enable=0 (swwel), so every relevant change implies a new trace start = a new config message

2.name: CFG_ON_SYNC
2.desc: Like CFG_ONCE, plus one config message after every periodic sync

fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: Context
fields.desc:
Send Ownership messages (TCODE 2) to indicate processor context:
emitted on a context-report ingress event (ctype != 0), on a
privilege-level change between retires, and after every
synchronizing message (N-Trace 7.1). PROCESS payload =
{CONTEXT, V, PRV, FORMAT} per Table 13. [CTTE granularity;
TCODE 2 itself is N-Trace standard]
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: InstSeqSyncEnable
fields.desc:
Emit a full synchronization message with SYNC=4 (Sequential
Instruction Counter) when the internal instruction-count
accumulator reaches its cap, instead of the bandwidth-lean
ResourceFull(RCODE=0) drain. CAUTION: N-Trace 1.0 allows SYNC=4
only in BTM mode; enabling it in the HTM-only CTTE is a
documented Accemic extension (any decoder still treats it as a
full re-anchor). Reset 0 = RCODE-0 drains (strictly N-Trace).
Applies to the composer-side pre-drain (the dominant path for
long linear runs); msg_gen-internal drains stay RCODE-0. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: InstTrigEnable
fields.desc:
Enable instruction trace trigger: while set, a pulse on the
generic tip.trigger event input upgrades the next retire to a
synchronization message with SYNC=6 (Trace Event / watchpoint
marker, N-Trace Table 25). Integrators wire tip.trigger to a
core watchpoint unit or external trigger fabric; the MBV
adapter ties it 0 (integration requirement, see
doc/supported_configurations.md).
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: InstStallOrOverflow
fields.desc:
Sticky status: set when the encoder generated an OVERFLOW message,
i.e. when the eTIP drop path discarded messages and injected the
Error(QueueOverrun) marker (N-Trace Required status bit).
Write 1 to clear (RW1C); additionally cleared by hardware while
trTeControl.Enable = 0, so every trace session starts from a
known-clear bit. Pure status -- setting or clearing it has NO
effect on the wire stream.
STALL HALF NOT IMPLEMENTED: the second half of the standard
semantics ('or TE requests hart stall') needs a back channel to
the hart. The CTTE ingress port (rtl/pkg/tip_if.sv) is
UNIDIRECTIONAL -- there is no stall/ready signal towards the
core -- so no CTTE adapter can stall a hart and the companion
control bit trTeControl.InstStallEna [13] stays unimplemented
(see the commented stub below). The bit therefore reports
overflow only. [N-Trace Required, overflow half]
fields.access_rule: write-1-to-clear: a read-modify-write of the whole register clears this bit unintentionally

fields.name: InhibitSrc
fields.desc:
Add source field to trace message.
Only accessible on trTeControl. Enable=0
fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

fields.name: InstSyncMode
fields.desc:
Periodic instruction trace synchronization mode.
This field combines bits 17 and 16 (standard trTeInstSyncMode) with the two reserved bits 19 and 18.
Only accessible on trTeControl. Enable=0

0.name: ITR_SYNC_OFF
0.desc: No periodic instruction trace synchronization message/packet generation

1.name: ITR_SYNC_TRACE_MSG
1.desc:
Count emitted trace messages: on-wire message boundaries as they
leave the encoder egress (ATB flush pseudo-messages do not count).
A synchronization message is requested once 2^(InstSyncMax+4)
messages were emitted since the last sync. With CT_EN_QUOTA_SYNC=0
the mode stays writable but has no effect (no sync is generated).

3.name: ITR_SYNC_HALFWORDS
3.desc: Count instruction half-words (16-bit)

4.name: ITR_SYNC_TRACE_BYTES
4.desc:
Count emitted trace bytes as accepted on the ATB output: whole
output beats, so alignment padding and flush idle beats count
toward the quota. A synchronization message is requested once
2^(InstSyncMax+4) bytes were emitted since the last sync -- the
bound a live/ring-buffer consumer programs to make the maximum
re-anchor distance a fixed number of bytes. With
CT_EN_QUOTA_SYNC=0 the mode stays writable but has no effect.

fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

fields.name: InstSyncMax
fields.desc:
Maximum interval between sync messages (2^(trTeInstSyncMax+4)).
The unit follows InstSyncMode: on-wire trace messages (mode 1),
hart clock cycles (2), instruction half-words (3), emitted ATB
trace bytes (4), wallclock cycles (5) or instructions (6).

Resets to 6, i.e. a period of 2^(6+4) = 1024 units in
whichever unit InstSyncMode selects. The reset value matters
because the natural programming path is ONE write to
trTeControl ('periodic sync, counted in X'), which takes the
mode from software and the period from here. 1024 is the knee
of the measured cost curve: the periodic sync then costs 2.5 %
of the trace stream, while every wider period can save at most
those 2.5 % and doubles the blind window of a consumer that
attaches mid-stream. The minimum period (0 = every 16 units)
costs a factor 2.4 on the same workload and loses trace against
a finite sink -- it remains available as an explicit stress
configuration, but it is not a product default (P0-02;
gate tests/instruction/37_sync_cadence -- the raw
measurement behind those numbers is not part of this
repository).
Only accessible on trTeControl. Enable=0
fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

fields.name: Format
fields.desc:
Trace recording format.
Only accessible on trTeControl. Enable=0

1.name: TR_FORMAT_N
1.desc: N-Trace messages with 6 MDO + 2 MSEO bits

fields.access_rule: read-only

fields.name: InstSyncReq
fields.desc:
Explicit instruction-trace synchronization request (TCI trTeInstSyncReq).
Write-1 semantics: the write raises ONE request and the field clears
itself in the next cycle, so it always reads back 0. The request is
served by the sync generator on the first qualifying retired
instruction and appears on the wire as the explicit-request code
SYNC = 14 -- the same code the ACT-CAP CF_SYNC command and the ATB
sync-request input produce, because the source is irrelevant to a
decoder (every synchronization message is a full re-anchor). For
diagnosis the source is recorded in trTeSyncStatus.SyncReqSource
(value 4, SYNC_REQ_TE).
Deliberately NOT gated on trTeInstSyncMode: unlike the ATB request
(mode 7) this field is itself the trigger and works in every cadence
mode. A request written while instruction tracing is paused is
DEFERRED, not dropped: it is served after the resume anchor.
Request depth is one in flight plus one remembered: a write arriving
while a request is still outstanding is NOT swallowed -- it is
launched as its own request as soon as the outstanding one has been
served and produces its OWN synchronization message. Only a write
that arrives when a request is already waiting to be launched
collapses into it (it asks for what is about to be asked anyway).
Measured on the system test (scripts/cli_tesyncreq_test.sh, legs
req/req2/req3): one write -> 1 SYNC = 14, two writes back to back ->
2, three writes back to back -> 2.
Requires the CT_EN_INST_SYNC_REQ build switch; without it the write
is still accepted and still auto-clears, but nothing consumes it
(the pre-2026-08 behaviour). [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: write-1 pulse: self-clearing, always reads back 0

fields.name: SendDeviceId
fields.desc:
Send a Device ID message (Nexus TCODE 1, IEEE-ISTO 5001 4.3.2)
carrying the encoder instance's static identifier (elaboration
parameter CT_DEVICE_ID of ct_encoder; layout per ISTO Table B-5
RN | PN | MID), so a stock Nexus decoder learns which device
produced the stream without out-of-band setup.
Resets to DID_NONE -- deliberately UNLIKE SendConfig: N-Trace 1.0
does not adopt TCODE 1 (Table 9), so the default stream stays
strictly N-Trace 1.0 and byte-identical to the pre-P4 reference.
Requires the CT_EN_DEVICE_ID build switch; profiles without the
feature read DID_NONE.
Bit position: the CTTE-vendor area above InstSyncReq -- bits
[13:12] are reserved for the standard TE status/stall fields
(trTeInstStallOrOverflow / trTeInstStallEna, see the commented
stubs above). [CTTE specific]

0.name: DID_NONE
0.desc: Do not send a Device ID message

1.name: DID_ONCE
1.desc: Send one Device ID message per trace-on edge (rising edge of effective instruction tracing), before the config message and before the first synchronizing message. NOT once per session: after an instruction-tracing pause the message is sent again -- same trigger as SendConfig=CFG_ONCE, and what a decoder attaching during the pause needs

fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

regs.name: Sync Request Status Register
regs.desc:
Diagnostic status for explicit synchronization requests. On the wire
every explicit sync request is emitted with the single vendor SYNC
code 14 (explicit sync request) -- N-Trace 1.0 Table 25 reserves
codes 10-13 for future standard use, so the former per-source codes
12 (CSR) and 13 (ATB) are no longer used. The request source does
not matter to a decoder (every synchronization message is a full
re-anchor); it is kept readable here for diagnosis. [CTTE specific]

fields.name: SyncReqSource
fields.desc: Source of the most recent explicit synchronization request. [CTTE specific]

0.name: SYNC_REQ_NONE
0.desc: No explicit sync request since reset

1.name: SYNC_REQ_CSR
1.desc:
Most recent explicit sync request came from the traced hart itself:
an ACT-CAP CF_SYNC command written to CPU CSR 0x0B10

2.name: SYNC_REQ_ATB
2.desc: Most recent explicit sync request came from the ATB sync request input

3.name: SYNC_REQ_QUOTA
3.desc:
Most recent explicit sync request came from a trace-quota counter
overflow (InstSyncMode 1/4 threshold 2^(InstSyncMax+4) reached
on the trace output)

4.name: SYNC_REQ_TE
4.desc:
Most recent explicit sync request came from the control bus:
a write of 1 to trTeControl.InstSyncReq (CT_EN_INST_SYNC_REQ).
Kept distinct from SYNC_REQ_CSR because the requester is a
different actor -- the external control/debug bus, not the
traced hart

fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: eTIP FIFO Fill Histogram Control
regs.desc:
Control for the SERIAL fill-level histogram read-out via
trTeTipFifoHistData. The number of bins (CT_FIFO_HIST_BINS,
default 16) is an RTL parameter -- the CSR map is
independent of it (one data register, serial pointer).
[CTTE specific]

fields.name: HistClear
fields.desc:
Write 1 to clear all histogram counters AND the read
pointer and hold them at 0, write 0 to re-arm. Level,
no CDC -- change only while the trace is quiescent
(trTeControl.Enable=0). [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: freely writable

fields.name: RdRewind
fields.desc:
Write 1 to rewind the serial read pointer to bin pair 0
WITHOUT clearing the counters (re-read the histogram).
Self-clearing. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: write-1 pulse: self-clearing, always reads back 0

fields.name: RdIdx
fields.desc:
Current serial read pointer (bin-pair index the next
trTeTipFifoHistData read will return). [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.name: eTIP FIFO Fill Histogram Data (serial read-out)
regs.desc:
SERIAL window into the CT_FIFO_HIST_BINS saturating 16-bit
upward-crossing counters (AW: not random access -- one
register, DSP-backed counters, minimal readback). Each read
returns bin pair [2*RdIdx (Lo), 2*RdIdx+1 (Hi)] and
auto-increments RdIdx (wraps after BINS/2). Bin b counts
crossings of fill level (b+1)*DEPTH/BINS, DEPTH =
ETIP_CVS_FIFO_DEPTH. Read protocol: HistClear or RdRewind,
then BINS/2 consecutive reads. No CDC -- read only while
the trace is quiescent (trTeControl.Enable=0). [CTTE specific]

fields.name: Lo
fields.desc: Bin 2*RdIdx   -- crossings of level (2*RdIdx+1)*DEPTH/BINS. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: reading has a side effect (see the register description)

fields.name: Hi
fields.desc: Bin 2*RdIdx+1 -- crossings of level (2*RdIdx+2)*DEPTH/BINS. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: read-only

regs.desc: Primary control register for the ATB Bridge.

fields.name: Active
fields.desc:
Primary activate/reset for the ATB Bridge. When 0, the ATB Bridge
may have clocks gated off or be powered down, and other register
locations may be inaccessible.
[Not implemented: read-only constant 1; there is no clock-gate/power-down control behind it.]

fields.name: Enable

regs.name: Watchpoint Message Mask Register
regs.desc: Enable mask for Watchpoint messages (Nexus TCODE 15). [CTTE specific]

fields.name: WEM
fields.desc:
Watchpoint Event Mask: one bit per reportable watchpoint slot.
A 1 ENABLES reporting of that bit (IEEE-ISTO 5001 Table B-26,
'WEM ... 1 = enabled'). NOTE: the prose of ISTO 4.3.23 says the
WPHIT field is 'masked by 1', which reads like the inverse; CTTE
follows Table B-26.
The emitted WPHIT of an ACT_CAP_ST_WATCHPOINT command is
Cmd.DirectData[15:0] AND WEM, so which slot owns which bit is a
SOFTWARE convention: program the watchpoints[] entry with the
DirectData bit you want to see and enable that bit here. A
command whose masked result is 0 emits no message.
Reset 0 masks every hit, so adding the feature to an existing
build changes no wire byte until software opts in. Writable only
while trTeControl.Enable=0. Requires the CT_EN_WATCHPOINT_MSG
build switch (which itself requires CT_EN_ACT); profiles without
the feature read 0.
fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

regs.name: Watchpoints Index Register
regs.desc:
Slot index for the indirect watchpoint load/readback path.
A trWpDataHigh write commits the staged entry to slot Idx and
then increments Idx; a trWpReadHigh read returns the shadow
entry at Idx and also increments it. Both wrap from
NUM_ACT_ST-1 back to 0. Software normally writes the start
slot once and streams NUM_ACT_ST Low/High pairs. Reads return
the CURRENT index, so after a burst of n commits starting at
i the register reads (i + n) mod NUM_ACT_ST -- cheap load
verification. Values >= NUM_ACT_ST are out of range: hardware
uses the low address bits and the first increment normalizes
to 0. The one in-window out-of-range value, Idx = NUM_ACT_ST
(= 1023), addresses the physical padding slot behind the last
tree node: a commit or readback there is inert for matching
(the search never visits that slot) and the following
increment wraps to 0. Writable only while
trTeControl.Enable=0. [CTTE specific]

fields.desc: Watchpoint slot index the next commit/readback targets. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

regs.name: Watchpoint Data Low (Addr staging)
regs.desc:
Address (PC) that arms the watchpoint entry being staged. When
the retired CPU PC matches Addr, the Cmd committed with it is
dispatched through the CTTE unit. Write Low first, then
trWpDataHigh -- the High write commits the pair to slot
trWpIndex.Idx; a Low write alone has no effect. Writable only
while trTeControl.Enable=0. [CTTE specific]

fields.name: Value
fields.desc: Addr (PC) to stage. [CTTE specific]
fields.access_rule: writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 -- a write while enabled is discarded WITHOUT an error response

regs.name: Watchpoint Data High (Cmd staging + COMMIT)
regs.desc:
Command of the watchpoint entry being staged. Writing this
register COMMITS {trWpDataLow, this word} to slot
trWpIndex.Idx and increments Idx -- identical commit semantics
to the historical +0x4 write of the removed 0x4100 window.
Bit layout is shared with RISC-V CSR 0x0B10 (ACT-CAP
protocol), which the CPU can write directly to dispatch the
same command immediately without going through the table.
Writable only while trTeControl.Enable=0 (the lock also
suppresses the commit).

Rules for programming the table:

  1. Fill ALL NUM_ACT_ST slots (trWpCap.Entries). Unused
     slots are not optional — leaving a slot at its reset
     value can mask real watchpoints.
  2. Addr values across slot 0 .. slot NUM_ACT_ST-1 must be
     strictly ascending and unique (Addr[i] < Addr[i+1]).
  3. Each slot is a pair: write trWpDataLow first, then this
     register. The High write is what commits the entry.
  4. Update the entire table with tracing disabled
     (trTeControl.Enable = 0). The index/staging registers
     are hardware-locked while enabled; a table changed
     mid-trace would produce undefined matches.

  5. Watchpoint messages (Cmd = ACT_CAP_ST_WATCHPOINT, Nexus
     TCODE 15): which BIT of the on-wire WPHIT field stands
     for which slot is a SOFTWARE convention, not hardware.
     Put the bit you want to see into that slot's
     DirectData[15:0] (one-hot is the obvious choice) and
     enable the same bit in trWpMask.WEM; the encoder emits
     WPHIT = DirectData[15:0] AND WEM and stays silent when
     that is 0.

For slots you do not need as real watchpoints, pick an Addr
the CPU will never execute (odd instruction addresses are
ideal — the core forces PC[0] = 0, so odd Addr values never
match) and set Cmd = ACT_CAP_ST_NONE. The Addr values of such
padding slots still have to satisfy rule 2. [CTTE specific]
